recipes.name: Punjabi chicken and spinach saag
steps: Fry cumin and chopped onion in the pot for 6 min until golden.
Add grated garlic and ginger, chopped tomato and the spices; cook 4 min.
Add chicken and 100 ml water; pressure cook on high for 8 min, natural release 5 min.
Stir in washed spinach until wilted, blend about half with a stick blender, simmer 5 min.
Cook rice separately in the rice cooker.
recipes.kid: Take the toddler portion out before adding salt and any chilli. Shred the chicken finely and blend the saag smooth.
recipes.lite: Serve over half the rice and add a side of cucumber and tomato salad.
recipes.store: Fridge 2 days, freezer 2 months. Cool rice within 1 hour and reheat only once.

recipes.name: Keema-stuffed bell peppers
steps: Cook chopped onion, garlic and ginger in ghee 5 min.
Add mince and spices and brown 8 min, add chopped tomato and cook until dry.
Halve and deseed the peppers, fill with keema.
Bake at 190 C for 25 min, or steam in the pressure cooker for 8 min.
Finish with fresh coriander.
recipes.kid: Serve the toddler soft keema and pepper strips separately, with the keema taken out before salt and chilli.
recipes.lite: Peppers are the carb here, so skip bread and rice and add a yogurt raita.

recipes.name: Keema-stuffed bitter gourd (karela)
steps: Cut the karela into 4 cm rings, scrape out the seeds, rub with salt and rest 20 min, then rinse and squeeze.
Brown onion, garlic and ginger, add mince, spices and tomato and cook until dry.
Stuff the rings with keema, lay in the pot with 100 ml water.
Pressure cook for 10 min, natural release.
Serve with roti.
recipes.kid: Bitter gourd is a strong flavour. Offer the toddler the keema filling with roti and a small piece of karela, no pressure.
recipes.lite: Karela is low calorie and high fibre; eat it with one roti and extra yogurt.

recipes.name: Beef or mutton nihari
steps: Fry sliced onion in ghee until deep brown, add ginger, garlic, masala and the meat, brown 5 min.
Add 900 ml water; pressure cook for 50 min, natural release.
Mix atta with 100 ml cold water, stir in and simmer 10 min until thick.
Top with ginger strips, coriander and lemon juice.
recipes.kid: Take the toddler portion before salt. Shred the meat finely and use plenty of gravy so it is easy to scoop. Remove any bone pieces.
recipes.lite: Rich: serve a smaller portion with a green salad and one roti.

recipes.name: Chicken shami kababs with rice
steps: Soak the dal 30 min. Pressure cook chicken, dal, onion, ginger, garlic and spices with 200 ml water for 15 min.
Drain any extra liquid, cool slightly, then pulse in the food processor to a coarse paste with the egg and mint.
Shape small flat patties.
Shallow-fry in 1 tbsp oil per batch, 3 min a side.
Cook rice separately.
recipes.kid: Make a few mini patties for the toddler, flat and soft, broken into pieces. Good finger food.
recipes.lite: Shallow-fry on a non-stick pan or bake at 200 C for 15 min.
recipes.store: Patties freeze well (2 months); separate with baking paper.

recipes.name: Punjabi rajma (kidney bean curry)
steps: Soak beans overnight, drain and rinse.
Fry cumin and onion in ghee, add garlic, ginger, tomato and spices until soft and oily.
Add beans and 700 ml water; pressure cook on high for 30 min, natural release.
Mash a few beans into the gravy and simmer 5 min.
Serve with rice.
recipes.kid: Beans must be fully soft; pressure cooking does this. Mash part of the beans for the toddler.
recipes.lite: High in fibre and protein; use half the rice.

recipes.name: Chicken yakhni pulao
steps: Pressure cook chicken with half the onion, ginger, garlic and whole spices in 900 ml water for 15 min to make the stock (yakhni).
Strain the stock and keep the chicken.
Fry the remaining sliced onion in ghee until brown, add the chicken and yogurt and cook 5 min.
Add soaked rice and 600 ml of the stock; cook until the water is absorbed, then steam on low 10 min.
recipes.kid: Shred the chicken, remove all bones and serve soft rice. Take the toddler portion before extra salt.
recipes.lite: Serve a smaller rice portion and add a raita and a plate of salad.
recipes.store: Fridge 2 days. Cool rice quickly and reheat only once.

recipes.name: Chana masala (spiced chickpea curry)
steps: Soak chickpeas overnight.
Fry cumin and onion, add garlic, ginger, tomato and spices until oily.
Add chickpeas and 600 ml water; pressure cook for 20 min, natural release.
Mash some chickpeas to thicken, finish with lemon juice.
recipes.kid: Squash or mash the chickpeas and serve with soft roti torn into small pieces.
recipes.lite: High fibre and protein; fill half the plate with salad.

recipes.name: Baked fish with spiced potatoes
steps: Cut potatoes into wedges, toss with half the oil and spices, roast at 200 C for 20 min.
Mix yogurt, garlic, lemon juice and spices; coat the fish.
Add the fish to the tray and bake 12 to 15 min.
Finish with coriander.
recipes.kid: Check the fish very carefully for bones and flake it. Serve potato wedges as finger food.
recipes.lite: Lean and high in protein; use half the potato and add roasted vegetables.
recipes.store: Fridge 1 day only. Reheat until piping hot.

recipes.name: Punjabi kadhi pakora (yogurt gravy)
steps: Whisk yogurt, 60 g besan, turmeric and 800 ml water until smooth, simmer 30 min stirring often.
Mix remaining besan with chopped onion, spinach, salt and a little water into a thick batter.
Fry or bake small spoonfuls (pakora) until crisp.
Temper oil with cumin and fenugreek, pour over the kadhi, add the pakora and serve with rice.
recipes.kid: Bake the toddler pakora at 200 C so they are less oily and cut them in half. Offer the kadhi mild.
recipes.lite: Bake the pakora instead of frying and use half the rice.
recipes.store: Fridge 2 days. Kadhi thickens, add water to reheat.

recipes.name: Degi style chicken or mutton korma
steps: Fry sliced onion in ghee until golden, add ginger, garlic, spices and meat; brown 8 min.
Whisk in yogurt a spoon at a time.
Add 150 ml water; pressure cook for 12 min (chicken) or 35 min (mutton).
Reduce until the oil separates.
recipes.kid: Take the toddler portion out before salt. Shred the meat; the sauce is mild and creamy.
recipes.lite: Rich: smaller portion, extra vegetables or salad, less ghee.

recipes.name: Lentil and beef shepherd's pie
steps: Brown the mince with onion and grated carrot.
Add lentils, tomato paste, thyme and 400 ml water; pressure cook for 8 min.
Boil and mash the potatoes with milk and butter.
Top the filling with mash and bake at 200 C for 20 min.
recipes.kid: Soft texture all over; add a spoon of the filling without salt before seasoning.
recipes.lite: Good for lighter eating: the lentils add fibre; use less mash and add peas.

recipes.name: Sheet pan chicken and pepper fajitas
steps: Slice the chicken, peppers and onion.
Toss with oil and spices on a sheet pan.
Roast at 220 C for 20 to 25 min.
Squeeze over lime; serve in warm tortillas with yogurt.
recipes.kid: Cut the chicken into thin strips and serve peppers soft and sliced. Tortillas torn into small pieces.
recipes.lite: Use one tortilla or lettuce wraps and extra peppers.

recipes.name: Teriyaki beef and broccoli stir-fry (halal, no mirin)
steps: Mix soy, honey, cornflour and 80 ml water.
Stir-fry beef in hot oil 3 min, set aside.
Stir-fry garlic, ginger, carrot and broccoli 4 min.
Return the beef, add the sauce and cook 2 min.
Serve over rice.
recipes.kid: Soy sauce is salty: take the toddler portion out before adding the sauce, then add a splash. Cut the broccoli small and cook it soft.
recipes.lite: Use half rice and double broccoli; cruciferous vegetables are fine cooked.
recipes.note: Uses no mirin or sake so it stays halal.

recipes.name: Baked salmon and potato fish cakes
steps: Boil and mash the potatoes. Bake the salmon at 200 C for 12 min and flake it, checking for bones.
Mix salmon, potato, egg, spring onion, herbs, lemon zest and salt.
Shape 8 cakes, coat in crumbs.
Bake at 200 C with a drizzle of oil for 20 min, turning once.
recipes.kid: Make small patties for the toddler. Flake and check for bones. Add no extra salt.
recipes.lite: Bake rather than fry and serve with a big salad.

recipes.name: Bhindi masala (okra) with roti
steps: Wash and dry the okra thoroughly, then cut into rounds.
Fry in 2 tbsp oil on medium heat 8 min until no longer sticky, set aside.
Fry cumin, onion, garlic; add tomato and spices.
Return the okra, cook covered 5 min.
Serve with roti.
recipes.kid: Cut the okra into small rounds, cooked soft. Torn roti makes easy finger food.
recipes.lite: Light, high fibre; use less oil and one roti each.

recipes.name: Aloo gobi and peas
steps: Fry cumin, onion, garlic and ginger, add tomato and spices.
Add diced potato, cauliflower florets and 100 ml water.
Pressure cook for 4 min, or simmer covered 20 min.
Stir in the peas and cook 3 min.
Serve with roti.
recipes.kid: Cook until soft, mash a little. Tear roti into small pieces.
recipes.lite: Cauliflower is a good low-carb swap: use more cauliflower than potato.

recipes.name: Sheet pan sweet potato and black bean quesadillas
steps: Cube and roast sweet potato with cumin and oil at 220 C for 20 min.
Mash lightly with beans and paprika.
Fill tortillas with the mixture and cheese.
Bake on a tray at 200 C for 10 min, turning once.
Serve with lime yogurt.
recipes.kid: Cut into small strips; the filling is soft and mild.
recipes.lite: One quesadilla with salad and extra beans.

recipes.name: Creamy spinach and potato pasta
steps: Boil the potato until soft and cook the pasta.
Blend potato, spinach, garlic, cream cheese, a little pasta water and lemon in the food processor.
Toss with the pasta and warm for 2 min.
Top with cheese.
recipes.kid: Choose fusilli or penne that toddlers can grip. Serve without extra salt.
recipes.lite: Use a smaller pasta portion and add peas and extra spinach.

recipes.name: One-pot broccoli and cheddar mac and cheese
steps: Simmer macaroni and finely chopped broccoli in milk and 200 ml water, stirring, for 12 min.
Stir in butter and cheese until creamy.
Add mustard and a small pinch of salt.
recipes.kid: Chop the broccoli very small. Cheese gives calcium; no extra salt for the toddler portion.
recipes.lite: Use less pasta and more broccoli; add a side salad.

recipes.name: Yellow moong and masoor dal tadka with rice
steps: Rinse the dal; pressure cook with turmeric, tomato and 800 ml water for 8 min.
Whisk smooth.
Heat ghee, fry cumin and sliced garlic until golden, pour over the dal.
Add lemon juice, serve with rice.
recipes.kid: Naturally soft. Add salt after taking the toddler portion.
recipes.lite: Lentils and rice together are filling; have half the rice and a salad.

recipes.name: Turkish red lentil soup (mercimek)
steps: Sauté onion in oil, add chopped potato, carrot, lentils, spices and 1 litre water.
Pressure cook for 8 min.
Blend smooth.
Add lemon juice, serve with toasted bread.
recipes.kid: Smooth and easy to spoon. Take the toddler portion before adding salt.
recipes.lite: Low calorie and filling; serve with one slice of bread and a boiled egg.

recipes.name: Anda bhurji (spiced scrambled eggs) with roti
steps: Fry cumin and onion 4 min, add tomato and spinach and cook 3 min.
Pour in beaten eggs with turmeric and stir gently until just set.
Serve with roti.
recipes.kid: Cook the eggs fully. Serve soft and torn roti.
recipes.lite: High protein; use one roti and extra vegetables.

recipes.name: Hummus plate with pita and vegetables
steps: Blend chickpeas, tahini, lemon, garlic, oil and a little water until smooth.
Cut pita into strips and vegetables into thin sticks (cherry tomatoes in quarters).
Arrange with cheese and hummus.
recipes.kid: Cut cherry tomatoes in quarters, cucumber in thin sticks, and thin cheese slices. Tahini is a sesame allergen.
recipes.lite: Fill the plate mostly with vegetables, one pita each.
recipes.store: Hummus keeps 4 days in the fridge.

recipes.name: Chicken salad wrap
steps: Shred the chicken and mix with yogurt, lemon and salt.
Fill wraps with the chicken, lettuce and cucumber slices.
recipes.kid: Cut into small strips; shred the chicken finely.
recipes.lite: Use lettuce leaves in place of the wrap if you want it lighter.

recipes.name: Cardamom and berry baked oats
steps: Grate the carrot. Blend or stir oats, milk, egg, carrot, spices and baking powder.
Fold in half the berries, pour into a dish and top with the rest.
Bake at 180 C for 25 to 30 min.
recipes.kid: Serve warm in soft squares. No honey or syrup needed.
recipes.lite: Higher in fibre; skip any added sugar and top with extra berries.
recipes.store: Fridge 3 days; reheat a portion in the microwave.

recipes.name: Anda shami paratha roll
steps: Warm the shami patties in a pan.
Beat and scramble the eggs over the patties until set.
Wrap in warm paratha and slice.
recipes.kid: Cut into 2 cm strips and keep the filling soft.
recipes.lite: Use roti rather than paratha and add sliced cucumber.

recipes.name: Masala omelet bites and hash browns
steps: Beat eggs with chopped tomato, spinach, cumin and salt; pour into a greased muffin tin.
Coarsely grate the potato, squeeze dry and shape into patties.
Bake the bites and hash browns at 200 C for 18 min.
recipes.kid: Finger food: cut the bites into quarters.
recipes.lite: Egg bites are high protein; have two bites and a small hash brown.
recipes.store: Fridge 2 days; freeze bites for a month.

recipes.name: Mango and coconut chia pudding
steps: Whisk chia seeds into the coconut milk and milk.
Chill overnight in the fridge.
Top with chopped mango.
recipes.kid: Stir well so there are no clumps; serve with a spoon. Honey is fine at this age.
recipes.lite: Skip honey and let the mango sweeten it.

recipes.name: Savory whole-wheat waffles
steps: Blend spinach with milk and eggs.
Whisk into flour, baking powder and salt.
Cook in a hot waffle iron until golden.
recipes.kid: Cut into fingers and serve with yogurt to dip.
recipes.lite: One waffle with yogurt and berries.
recipes.store: Freeze cooked waffles for 1 month; toast to reheat.

recipes.name: Mini oatmeal pancakes
steps: Blend oats, banana, eggs, milk and cinnamon.
Cook small spoonfuls in a lightly oiled pan 2 min a side.
recipes.kid: Bite-sized and soft; no extra sugar.
recipes.lite: Two small pancakes with Greek yogurt.

recipes.name: Weekend halwa puri (suji halwa with puri)
steps: Toast semolina in ghee until fragrant, add 400 ml hot water and sugar, stir until thick; flavour with cardamom.
Knead flour, a pinch of salt and water to a stiff dough, roll small rounds.
Deep-fry the puri a few at a time until puffed.
recipes.kid: Offer a small piece of puri and a spoon of halwa; fried and sweet, so keep portions tiny.
recipes.lite: A treat: one puri, a small spoon of halwa and the chana masala.

recipes.name: Potato and chickpea tots
steps: Boil the potato until soft.
Pulse with the chickpeas and cumin.
Shape small tots and bake at 200 C for 20 min.
recipes.kid: Soft finger food; break open to check they are not too hot.

recipes.name: Hummus with pita strips and cherry tomatoes
steps: Cut the pita into strips and cherry tomatoes into quarters.
Serve the hummus as a dip.
recipes.kid: Quarter tomatoes lengthwise; check pita is soft.

recipes.name: Date and oat energy balls
steps: Process dates, oats and cinnamon to a sticky dough.
Roll into small balls and coat in coconut.
recipes.kid: Sticky and sweet: offer only one small ball with water, and brush teeth after.

recipes.name: Steamed carrot and apple wedges with yogurt dip
steps: Steam carrot sticks and thin apple wedges for 4 min until soft.
Cool and serve with yogurt.
recipes.kid: Both softened, thin strips; never raw hard carrot or apple pieces.

recipes.name: Baked spinach and potato roll-ups
steps: Mash boiled potato with wilted spinach and cheese.
Spread on wraps, roll up tightly.
Bake at 200 C for 12 min and cut into pinwheels.
recipes.kid: Cut pinwheels in half.

recipes.name: Whole-wheat banana oat muffins
steps: Mash bananas, mix with egg and milk.
Add oats, flour and baking powder.
Fill muffin cases and bake at 180 C for 20 min.
recipes.kid: Soft, naturally sweet. Cut in half.

recipes.name: Ripe melon pieces with yogurt
steps: Cut melon into small soft pieces.
Serve with yogurt.
recipes.kid: Small soft pieces only.

recipes.name: Unsalted whole-wheat crackers and cheese
steps: Shred or thinly slice the cheese.
Serve with crackers.
recipes.kid: Shred or slice cheese thinly; crumble the crackers if needed.

recipes.name: Banana yogurt wrap
steps: Spread yogurt over the wrap, add banana and roll.
Slice into pinwheels.
recipes.kid: Cut pinwheels in half.

recipes.name: Cottage cheese with pineapple
steps: Chop the pineapple very small.
Spoon over the cottage cheese.
recipes.kid: Chop pineapple fine; tinned in juice, not syrup.

recipes.name: Berry and yogurt parfait
steps: Layer yogurt, mashed berries and oats.
Serve with a spoon.
recipes.kid: Halve blueberries and strawberries; mash raspberries.

recipes.name: Mango kulfi gelato
steps: Blend all ingredients until smooth.
Chill, then churn in the ice cream machine 25 min.
Freeze 1 hour to firm up.
recipes.kid: A small scoop (two tablespoons). Sweetened lightly with honey rather than condensed milk.
recipes.lite: Treat portion; one scoop.

recipes.name: Strawberry yogurt and honey frozen custard
steps: Blend strawberries, yogurt, milk and honey.
Churn in the ice cream machine 20 min.
recipes.kid: Small scoop; naturally sweetened.
recipes.lite: One scoop.

recipes.name: Cocoa swirl gelato
steps: Blend banana, milk, yogurt and honey.
Swirl in the cocoa and churn 25 min.
recipes.kid: A small scoop; cocoa has a little caffeine, so keep to a tablespoon or two.
recipes.lite: One scoop.

recipes.name: Mango lassi and berry spinach smoothie
steps: Blend everything until smooth.
Serve in an open cup or a straw cup.
recipes.kid: Offer a small cup (about 100 ml) with a snack. Serve in an open cup or straw cup.
recipes.lite: No honey needed; add ice only if you want it thicker.

recipes.name: Espresso latte (adult) and babyccino (toddler)
steps: Pull the espresso shot(s) for the adults.
Steam the milk.
Pour foam and a splash of warm milk into a small cup for the toddler.
recipes.kid: The babyccino is warm milk foam only, with no coffee. Check the temperature first.
recipes.lite: Use less milk; skip syrups.

portions.title: Meals and snacks
portions.text: Offer 3 meals (¾ to 1 cup of food per meal) and 2 snacks. Share family meals with your toddler. Start with small portions, such as 2 tablespoons of each food, and offer more if they are still hungry.
portions.src: Family Meal Planning and Toddler Nutrition Guide

portions.title: Milk
portions.text: Whole cow's milk is the usual choice from 12 months, because fat supports brain development until 24 months. Use cups, not bottles, and limit milk to 16 to 24 oz (about 475 to 700 ml) a day so there is room for solid food.
portions.src: Family Meal Planning and Toddler Nutrition Guide

portions.title: Added sugar
portions.text: Naturally occurring sugars in fruit and milk are not added sugars. Added sugars include brown sugar, corn syrup and honey. Check labels, limit juice, and choose cereals with minimal added sugar.

safety.title: Choking prevention
safety.text: Chop or grind whole nuts, cut hard raw vegetables into thin strips or cook until soft, halve small round foods (blueberries) and quarter larger ones (grapes, cherry tomatoes), thinly slice hard fruit like apple, shred or thinly slice cheese, spread nut and seed butters thinly, and avoid popcorn and hard or sticky sweets.
safety.src: Family Meal Planning and Toddler Nutrition Guide

safety.title: Salt in family cooking
safety.text: Set the toddler portion aside before adding salt, stock cubes, soy sauce or ready-made masala mixes, then season the rest for the adults.

safety.title: Iron
safety.text: Pair iron-rich foods (meat, lentils, beans, chickpeas, spinach) with vitamin C (lemon, tomato, peppers) and avoid tea with meals.

safety.title: Rice and leftovers
safety.text: Cool cooked rice within an hour, keep it in the fridge, eat within a day or two and reheat only once until steaming hot.

safety.title: Beans
safety.text: Dried kidney beans must be boiled until fully soft. Pressure cooking does this; never use a slow cooker for raw kidney beans.

safety.title: Fish
safety.text: Check fillets for bones. Avoid shark, swordfish and marlin for toddlers, and serve fish no more than a couple of times a week.

safety.title: Allergens
safety.text: Egg, fish, sesame (tahini), dairy, wheat and nuts are all in this plan. Each recipe lists its allergens. If you avoid an ingredient, add it in Setup and the planner will skip any recipe that contains it.

safety.title: Halal
safety.text: Meat is assumed halal. The teriyaki uses no mirin or sake, and no recipe uses alcohol-based flavouring.

rhythm.title: Cook three nights, eat well all week
rhythm.text: Sun, Tue and Thu are batch-cook nights: one big pot covers that night, the next night, and a packed lunch. Sat is a quick 30-minute meal. Mon, Wed and Fri are reheat nights, so you cook three times, not seven.

rhythm.title: Toddler day
rhythm.text: On childcare days the toddler eats breakfast and an afternoon snack at home, and lunch at childcare. Dinner is the family meal at home.

rhythm.title: Adult lunch
rhythm.text: Lunch after a batch-cook night is the leftover. Work-from-home days get a quick fresh lunch from a short rotation (dal, soup, bhurji, hummus plate, wrap).

rhythm.title: Lighter plates
rhythm.text: For lighter eating, fill half the plate with vegetables or salad, use about half the usual rice or bread, keep a palm-sized portion of protein, and use less ghee or oil. Every recipe has a one-line lighter tip.
